name: b-crosshatched-grin-closeup
prompt: Tall portrait pen-and-ink drawing on cream paper, black ink only: an enormous jowly face of a rich gentleman crammed edge to edge, so near that his ears are cropped off and no park, sky or room shows behind him. A black silk top hat brim runs flat along the top border like a lid. Beneath it his brow and both eye hollows are built from short overlapping cross-hatched strokes, laid in patches going different directions, piled until they go almost solid black; on the cheeks and nose the hatching loosens into fine stipple dots like grain in skin. One eye catches a hard white glint and is drawn with unnerving care, every lash and wet fold; curved inside that glint is a tiny mirrored figure, a worn-out nurse in creased scrubs slouched on a wooden park bench, the sole other person anywhere in the picture. His mouth is a polite smile stretched far too wide, thin lips, a neat row of small identical teeth, fat cheeks bunching up into hatched creases. Scratchy nib marks, slightly broken lines, ink pressure heavy and obsessive. Below his chins and stiff wing collar the drawing simply stops, leaving a broad band of clean empty paper along the lower edge. Straight-on eye-level view, uncomfortably close, flat even light with every shadow made by pen strokes rather than lighting. No grey wash, no colour, no words or letters. Thanks.
